title: Quick Deploy Guided Flow — Pricing Framing & Snippets (draft)
body:
Purpose: fast, consumable messaging that product/marketing and SDKs can use to push a one-click or 1-minute integration experience. Focus: developer-first value props, concrete quickstart script, and compact pricing language that reduces friction and surprises.

Topline positioning hypothesis (single sentence): Redwood Hosted API gets teams from prototype to production-grade inference in minutes — low cognitive load, transparent unit economics, and smooth scale to reserved capacity when you’re ready.

Why this doc: engineers want concrete steps and predictable cost signals. current GTM copy is feature-forward; this draft flips to a legible flow: (1) integrate, (2) measure latency/cost, (3) choose efficiency levers.

Core developer-first value props (short bulleted lines for microcopy):
- Start in minutes: single SDK call + sample prompt.
- Predictable token economics: per-token metering with cost preview in the console.
- Drop-in performance: streaming & batching enabled by default for low latency.
- Path to scale: reserve Dedicated capacity with one click once you hit production throughput.
- Observable by design: route-level latency & cost breakdowns so you never guess.

Quickstart flow (three variants: PoC, MVP, Production-ready) — copy + engineer checklist snippets:
1) PoC (60–90 seconds):
- Microcopy: "Try infer in your terminal: npm i @redwood/infer && node quickstart.js — see a generated reply in <2s."
- Checklist: grab API key, run example script, confirm output. No billing surprises: first 20k tokens free credit.
- Hook for README: "One file to rule them all — get an answer in under a minute."

2) MVP (10–30 minutes):
- Microcopy: "Wire up SDK, enable streaming, and add a simple retry policy. Preview cost before you hit production."
- Checklist: integrate SDK in app, set streaming=true, run integration tests, open Console > Routes to view latency/cost per-call.
- Tip: turn on KV prefix caching for chat-heavy workloads (1-click in Console).

3) Production-ready (hours to roll out):
- Microcopy: "Pin a production model, configure autoscale, and opt for Reserved capacity if you want guaranteed throughput and lower unit costs."
- Checklist: model pin, rollout policy (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%), enable tracing, set SLOs and alerting.

Pricing language — short statements for UI, docs, and marketing (simple, non-legal):
- Headline: "Simple, usage-based pricing — pay per token, scale with reserved capacity."
- Short explainer: "Hosted: pay per token for on-demand access. Reserved: commit monthly for lower per-token rates and guaranteed throughput."
- How to preview: "Estimate cost in Console before you run heavy workloads. Console shows per-route token estimate and 7-day cost projection."
- Cost guardrails: "Set route-level caps to avoid runaway bills; get notifications at 50%, 80%, 100% of forecasted spend."

Pricing microcopy variants (for A/B tests):
A) "Pay only for what you use. No commitments to start."
B) "Start free, pay as you scale — optional Reserved capacity for predictable costs."
C) "Per-token pricing, with automatic batching & caching to lower your bill without code changes."

Competitive notes (quick, rough):
- Competitor A: blunt simplicity, cheap entry price, but lacks developer-grade telemetry and dev-facing quickstarts. Our advantage: telemetry + predictable scale path.
- Competitor B: strong on model catalog, weak on cost transparency. Our advantage: console cost previews + route-level breakdowns.
- Competitor C: low-latency edge offering; we compete on batching/cost curves and dedicated capacity SLAs.

Objection handling / FAQ snippets (for sales and docs):
Q: "How do I avoid unexpected bills?"
A: "Console cost preview + route caps + free starter credits — plus alerts at usage thresholds. You can also move hot paths to Reserved capacity for predictable pricing."

Q: "Is performance comparable to self-hosting?"
A: "For most applications, yes — our runtime picks kernels and batching strategies optimized per workload. For specialized latency SLAs, Dedicated deployments are available."

Suggested Console UX copy (compact):
- Estimate button: "Preview cost"
- Cap toggle: "Set route cap"
- Reserve CTA: "Reserve capacity — save up to X%" (X replaced by actual tier numbers in final)

Microcopy playbook (short snippets to drop into README, Slack templates, onboarding emails):
- README: "Run: node quickstart.js — get a reply in <2s. Free credits included."
- Slack DM for activation: "Congrats — your first infer ran in 42ms. See cost preview in Console -> Routes."
- Email subject (activation): "Your Redwood Hosted API is live — estimate your first month in Console"

Open questions / TODOs (callouts we need to resolve before final):
- Decide exact free credit amount and where to display it in microcopy (console vs. email).
- Finalize percent savings copy for Reserved capacity CTA (legal needs actual numbers).
- Clarify whether "first 20k tokens free" should be universal or limited to new signups only. Align with finance.
- Get engineering input on default batching/caching toggles (are they on by default for new projects?).

Experiments to run (priority ranking):
1) A/B test pricing microcopy A vs C on pricing page clickthrough to sign-up.
2) Measure activation funnel time: sample script run -> console preview opened -> first production call. Goal: <10 minutes for 50% of new projects.
3) In-UI experiment: show cost projection inline on quickstart page vs hidden behind "Preview cost" — measure conversion and confusion metrics.

Notes to design/docs: provide 3 short hero banners for web: (1) "Get an answer in under a minute" (developer), (2) "From prototype to SLA-backed throughput" (platform), (3) "Predictable pricing as you scale" (finance).

Rough draft CTA language for landing page: "Try Hosted API — free credits, one-line integration, transparent costs."

Appendix: example quickstart code snippet (for README/SDK site) — to be finalized with engineering: 
- JS: "const r = new Redwood({ key: process.env.RW_KEY }); const out = await r.generate({ model: 'rw-infer-small', prompt: 'Summarize this paragraph' }); console.log(out);"

Style notes: keep microcopy concrete, measurable, and action-oriented. Avoid vague superlatives ("best", "fastest") without benchmark links. Always pair product claims with what to do next ("Run quickstart", "Preview cost").

Owner notes and next steps:
- Aisha: coordinate finance for free credit language and reserved discounts (due 2026-03-15).
- Ben: sync with eng to confirm default batching & sample snippet accuracy (due 2026-03-12).
- Leah: produce 3 hero banner options for design review (due 2026-03-18).

End—this is intentionally concise and conversational. Use as source for landing page microcopy, Console UX labels, onboarding emails, and SDK README examples. Keep iterations in Drive; finalize after finance & engineering signoff.
